name: Starter: Basque
about: Basque in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Basque order.

words.ni: I, me (nik: I, doing something to something; nirekin: with me; niri: to me)
words.ukan: have (dut, duzu, du; ditut, ditu: with more than one)
words.zu: you (zuk: you, doing something to something)
words.izan: be (naiz, zara, da, gara, dira; zait: is to me)
words.pixka: bit, small amount (pixka bat: a little)

kontua-mesedez.about: Literally the account, please; mesedez is please.

wrong: Ni kafea eta tea edaten dut.
Ni kafea eta tea edaten ditut.
Ni tea eta ura edaten dut.
Ni tea eta ura edaten ditut.
Ni ura eta kafea edaten dut.
Ni ura eta kafea edaten ditut.

items.text: Te bat eta ur bat, mesedez.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: Tea bat eta ur bat, mesedez.
Te bat eta ura bat, mesedez.

items.means: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
Excuse me, how much is it?

items.text: Euskaraz pixka bat hitz egiten dut.
wrong: Euskaraz pixka bat hitz egiten naiz.
Euskaraz pixka bat hitz egiten ditut.

items.means: I live in a small house.
My mother goes to the city.
Tomorrow I'm going to the city.
The tall girl is my friend.
The keys are on the table.
There's no milk in the fridge.
We live in a big house.
I want to drink some water.
What do you want to eat?
Excuse me, where's the train station?
I'm going to the movies tonight.
I go to work by bus.
We're going to the mountains on Saturday.
We have to take a taxi.
What are you doing this weekend?
My parents live in San Sebastián.
I'm going to dinner with friends.
I talk to my mom every day.

words.means: dut = I have; ditut = I have

concept.line: The verb usually comes last, with its helper word after it: Nire laguna Bilbon bizi da (my friend in-Bilbao living is).
A question word goes right before the verb: Non dago tren geltokia?

words.means: naiz = I am; zara = you are; da = is

concept.line: izan says who or what someone is: naiz (am), zara (are), da (is), gara (we are), dira (they are): Nire ama irakaslea da (my mom teacher-the is).
-n is in or at, -ra is to and -tik is from, joined to the end of the place: etxean (in the house), etxera (to the house), etxetik (from the house).

words.means: bit, small amount (pixka bat: a little)

concept.line: A verb ending in -tzen or -ten with its helper (naiz for coming and going, dut for doing something to something) says what you usually do or what's the case now: Autobusez joaten naiz (by-bus going I-am), Ez dut ulertzen (not I-have-it understanding); ari picks out an action in progress.

words.means: etxe = house; etxean = in the house
joaten = go; zoaz = you are going

concept.line: -ren says whose, and comes before what's owned; my and your are nire and zure: lagunaren etxea (friend-the's house-the), nire ama (my mom).

words.means: joan = go; noa = I am going
